statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail. It holds that len(r) = n. Define: u is a substring of s iff u is non-empty and there exists p with 0 <= p <= len(s)-len(u) such that for all t with 0 <= t < len(u), u[t] = s[p+t]. Define u <=lex v to be the usual lexicographic order on byte arrays: u is a prefix of v (including u = v), or at the first index k where u and v differ, u[k] < v[k], comparing bytes as natural numbers. Then for every i with 0 <= i < n: if there exists a byte array u that is a substring of arr[i] and is not a substring of arr[j] for every j with 0 <= j < n and j != i, then r[i] is a substring of arr[i], r[i] is not a substring of any arr[j] with j != i, len(r[i]) <= len(u) for every such u, and r[i] <=lex u for every such u with len(u) = len(r[i]). If no such u exists, then r[i] is the empty byte array.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input arr satisfies the problem constraints: 2 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= len(arr[i]) <= 20 and every byte of arr[i] is in {97,...,122} (lowercase English letters). Indices are 0-based.
